instructions: Rinse 6 tbsp sweet rice in a bowl until the water runs mostly clear. Cover with cold water and soak for 1 to 2 hours, then drain.
Rinse the hens and pat them dry. Trim off any loose fat at the neck and tail. Slice the ginger into 4 thin coins. Cut the white parts off the scallions and set the green parts aside.
Stuff each hen with 2 tbsp of the rice, 2 jujubes, 5 garlic cloves, 2 ginger slices and 1 piece of ginseng. Cross the legs and tie them with kitchen twine.
Put the hens in a pot just big enough to hold them and add the last 2 tbsp of rice, the scallion whites and the peppercorns. Add 8 cups cold water, enough to cover the hens.
Bring to a boil over medium-high heat. Skim off the foam as it rises. Cover and cook for 20 minutes.

Turn the heat to medium-low and simmer, covered, for 25 minutes, skimming now and then. You're cooking the hens to 165°F in the thickest part of the thigh, so if you have a thermometer, check it there. No thermometer? Cut into the thickest part: it's done when the juices run clear.
Slice the scallion greens. Taste the soup. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve each person a hen or half a hen in a deep bowl, ladled with broth and topped with the scallion greens. Set out a small bowl of salt and pepper for seasoning at the table.
advance_prep_notes: soak the sweet rice for 1 to 2 hours ahead
method_notes: Posh Journal, Beyond Kimchee and Two Plaid Aprons agree on a small bird stuffed with soaked glutinous rice, garlic, jujube and ginseng, then simmered in plain water until the rice is cooked and the broth turns milky. They differ on bird (Cornish hens or a small whole chicken), herb kit versus fresh ginseng, and cooking time (45 minutes to 1 1/2 hours). None had 20 ratings (Posh Journal 4.92 from 12 votes, Beyond Kimchee 5 from 3, Two Plaid Aprons 5 from 2), so this is a fallback. This version follows Posh Journal with 2 hens for 4. Fresh ginseng comes from Korean grocers; dried ginseng root works.
